#3714546 [user] # Vendored zstd

Upstream: https://github.com/facebook/zstd
Version:  v1.5.7
Files:    zstd.c is the upstream single-file amalgamation, generated by
          `build/single_file_libs/create_single_file_library.sh` from the
          release tarball; zstd.h is lib/zstd.h verbatim.

The amalgamation is used rather than the ~40-file lib/ tree because cgo
    10|only compiles C sources in the package directory itself, and zstd's
sources use relative includes across common/ and compress/. It defines
ZSTD_MULTITHREAD internally, so ZSTD_c_nbWorkers works without extra
build flags — which is the whole reason for binding to C at all.

Licensed BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE.zstd). zstd is dual-licensed BSD-3-Clause
OR GPLv2; we take the BSD option, which is compatible with mnemo's
Apache-2.0. The GPLv2 alternative is deliberately NOT exercised and its
COPYING file is deliberately not vendored.

    20|## Updating

    curl -sL -o zstd.tar.gz https://github.com/facebook/zstd/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/zstd-X.Y.Z.tar.gz
    tar xzf zstd.tar.gz && cd zstd-X.Y.Z/build/single_file_libs && sh create_single_file_library.sh
    cp zstd.c <repo>/internal/zstdc/zstd.c
    cp ../../lib/zstd.h <repo>/internal/zstdc/zstd.h
    cp ../../LICENSE <repo>/internal/zstdc/LICENSE.zstd

Then update the version above and run the package tests.

#3714549 [user] // Copyright 2026 Marcelo Cantos
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

package upgrade

import (
	"fmt"
	"sync"
)
    10|
// NoticeTracker records per-session upgrade banners so each session
// sees `mnemo upgraded vN -> vN+1` at most once (🎯T97.6).
type NoticeTracker struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	pending map[string]string // sessionID -> message
	shown   map[string]string // sessionID -> last delivered message (dedupe)
}

// NewNoticeTracker builds an empty tracker.
    20|func NewNoticeTracker() *NoticeTracker {
	return &NoticeTracker{
		pending: map[string]string{},
		shown:   map[string]string{},
	}
}

// FormatNotice builds the canonical upgrade banner text.
func FormatNotice(from, to string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("mnemo upgraded %s -> %s", formatV(from), formatV(to))
    30|}

// MarkSession queues a one-time notice for sessionID.
func (t *NoticeTracker) MarkSession(sessionID, from, to string) {
	if sessionID == "" || from == "" || to == "" {
		return
	}
	msg := FormatNotice(from, to)
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
    40|	if t.shown[sessionID] == msg {
		return // already delivered this upgrade
	}
	t.pending[sessionID] = msg
}

// MarkSessions queues the same notice for many sessions.
func (t *NoticeTracker) MarkSessions(sessionIDs []string, from, to string) {
	for _, id := range sessionIDs {
		t.MarkSession(id, from, to)
    50|	}
}

// Consume returns the pending notice for sessionID and clears it.
// ok is false when there is nothing to show.
func (t *NoticeTracker) Consume(sessionID string) (msg string, ok bool) {
	if sessionID == "" {
		return "", false
	}
	t.mu.Lock()
    60|	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	msg, ok = t.pending[sessionID]
	if !ok {
		return "", false
	}
	delete(t.pending, sessionID)
	t.shown[sessionID] = msg
	return msg, true
}

    70|// PendingCount is for tests/diagnostics.
func (t *NoticeTracker) PendingCount() int {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	return len(t.pending)
}

#3714550 [user] // Copyright 2026 Marcelo Cantos
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

package upgrade

import "testing"

func TestNoticeOncePerSession(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
    10|	tr := NewNoticeTracker()
	tr.MarkSession("s1", "0.61.0", "0.62.0")
	tr.MarkSession("s1", "0.61.0", "0.62.0") // duplicate mark
	msg, ok := tr.Consume("s1")
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("expected notice")
	}
	want := "mnemo upgraded v0.61.0 -> v0.62.0"
	if msg != want {
		t.Fatalf("got %q want %q", msg, want)
    20|	}
	if _, ok := tr.Consume("s1"); ok {
		t.Fatal("second consume must be empty")
	}
	// Re-mark same upgrade after shown → suppressed
	tr.MarkSession("s1", "0.61.0", "0.62.0")
	if tr.PendingCount() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("should not re-queue already shown upgrade")
	}
	// Newer upgrade can notify again
    30|	tr.MarkSession("s1", "0.62.0", "0.63.0")
	msg, ok = tr.Consume("s1")
	if !ok || msg != "mnemo upgraded v0.62.0 -> v0.63.0" {
		t.Fatalf("got %q ok=%v", msg, ok)
	}
}

func TestNoticeMarkSessions(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	tr := NewNoticeTracker()
    40|	tr.MarkSessions([]string{"a", "b", ""}, "1.0.0", "1.1.0")
	if tr.PendingCount() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("pending %d", tr.PendingCount())
	}
}

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  # Dry run. The real build fires on `release: published` — i.e. AFTER
  # the tag exists — so a build failure on a leg CI does not cover
  # forces a re-cut of the release. ci.yml builds ubuntu-latest and
  # windows-latest only; this workflow additionally builds darwin/arm64,
    10|  # linux/arm64 and windows/arm64 (cross, via llvm-mingw), and links
  # statically on Windows. Since 🎯T159 every one of those legs compiles
  # a vendored 2.1 MB libzstd amalgamation through cgo, so the
  # uncovered legs now carry real build risk. Dispatch this before
  # tagging: it builds and packages everything and skips only the
  # uploads.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
    20|
jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: macos-latest
            goos: darwin
            goarch: arm64
            ext: ""
    30|            archive: tar.gz
            cc: cc
            cxx: c++
            ar: ar
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            goos: linux
            goarch: amd64
            ext: ""
            archive: tar.gz
            cc: cc
    40|            cxx: c++
            ar: ar
          - os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            goos: linux
            goarch: arm64
            ext: ""
            archive: tar.gz
            cc: cc
            cxx: c++
            ar: ar
    50|          - os: windows-latest
            goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            ext: ".exe"
            archive: zip
            # -H=windowsgui so Scheduled-Task launch does not pop a
            # console window (console_windows.go re-attaches stdio
            # when launched from a shell). -extldflags "-static"
            # static-links the MinGW runtime so end users do not
            # need MinGW-w64 DLLs on their PATH.
    60|            ldflags_extra: '-H=windowsgui -extldflags "-static"'
            # windows-latest has MinGW-w64 GCC preinstalled; bare
            # names resolve via PATH.
            cc: gcc
            cxx: g++
            ar: ar

            # PATH via GITHUB_PATH, so these bare names resolve.
